items.title: What One Bad Night Of Sleep Did To My Blood Sugar
items.summary: Sleep and metabolic health are more connected than most people realize, and this was a chance to see it play out in real data while traveling. After a night with only 6 hours and 24 minutes of sleep, average glucose rose 10 points and waking glucose increased 3 points compared to a night with over 8 hours. Just one night of poor sleep can raise hunger hormones like ghrelin and elevate blood sugar, which is why consistent, high-quality sleep is one of the more overlooked levers for metabolic health, especially for women. #GlucoseMonitoring #SleepHealth #MetabolicHealth #FemaleLongevity #ContinuousGlucoseMonitor #WomensHealth #SleepScience

items.title: Why Do You Feel Hungry at Certain Times? | Hunger Signals Explained | Genomaxis #glp1
items.summary: Why do you feel hungry at certain times of the day? Your hunger isn't random—it is influenced by hormones, energy needs, and signals between your body and brain. In this video, we explain how hunger signals, ghrelin, and leptin help regulate hunger and fullness, and why everyone can experience hunger at different times. You'll learn: Why hunger signals change throughout the day What ghrelin does and why it is linked to hunger How leptin is involved in fullness signaling Why everyone's hunger rhythm can be different How appetite regulation relates to modern metabolic health research Understanding these signals can provide a better perspective on appetite regulation, hunger hormones, and weight management. Learn more about the science behind GLP-1 peptides and appetite regulation through Genomaxis.

items.summary: Hi HN, I’m Lloyd, one of two founders of RonanRx ( https://ronanrx.com/ ). We are building a vertically integrated pharmaceutical company with software for prescribing, telehealth, compounding, manufacturing, and delivery. We are starting with GLP-1s and peptides. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. Around the same time, I decided to try and lose the weight I had gained while building the factory. I ate nothing but chicken for six months. While this diet got some results, I plateaued. My doctor suggested tirzepatide, a GLP-1 medication. For me, losing weight was only the beginning. "Food noise" was gone. I showed less interest in other compulsive behavior. I stopped scrolling Instagram and quit biting my nails. But that was just the beginning. I was born with a congenital heart defect called aortic stenosis. items.title: Your Indoor Air May Be Working Against Your Health
items.summary: Air is one of our largest daily exposures and one of the easiest to ignore because you cannot see most pollutants. I do not think home optimization should begin with buying every gadget. It should begin with measurement. PM2.5, VOCs, humidity, and CO2 can reveal whether cooking, cleaning products, poor ventilation, smoke, or an overcrowded room are changing the air you breathe. Once you know the problem, interventions become more rational: ventilation when outdoor air is clean, source control, appropriate filtration, and regular maintenance. A plant may improve the feel of a room, but it should not replace filtration or ventilation. My approach is to make the environments where I spend the most time as supportive as realistically possible, rather than trying to control every exposure in the world. #IndoorAirQuality #HealthyHome #AirPollution #EnvironmentalHealth #Longevity

items.title: Starting Exercise During Pregnancy Is Not Too Late
items.summary: This myth needed to be retired a long time ago. Dr. Margie Davenport explains that women who were inactive before pregnancy and started moving during it saw a 40 percent reduction in pregnancy complications like gestational diabetes, preeclampsia, and gestational hypertension, a 67 percent reduction in depression risk, and no increase in miscarriage, small baby, or early baby risk. The old idea that you shouldn't start something new once you're pregnant just isn't supported by the data. #pregnancyexercise #womenshealth #longevity #prenatalfitness #exerciseinpregnancy
